transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Time: 10:00am PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (NovaRetail Head of ML), Mark Dawson (Infra Lead), Aisha Khan (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy): quick sync on caching pilot, noted hit rates improved to mid 70s with prefix caching; need to tune key composition to avoid PII leakage; infra wants memory caps and TTL guidance; next steps to run larger benchmark.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh this is the weekly caching sync — Samir from Redwood here, with Lena. how's everybody doing?
[00:08] Priya: Good, thanks. Busy week but things looking better with the sample set.
[00:11] Aisha: Yep, hi.
[00:12] Mark: Morning.
[00:14] Samir: Quick agenda — review last week's numbers, dig into prefix vs KV cache hit rates, discuss prompt-reuse / fingerprinting approach, and then action items. Sound good?
[00:21] Priya: Yep.
[00:23] Lena: All right, I'll start with the dashboard update — small caveat, I grabbed some extra logs which made the totals a bit noisy at first, sorry about that.
[00:32] Lena: So for the week, with prefix caching enabled on the pilot model (redwood-hosted variant), we see overall token-level cache hits around 72 to 78 percent depending on route. Prefix-only hit rate was about 81 percent on the support-ticket prompts, while KV cache (session-level KV) was lower, around 46 percent, which matches expectation because session variability is higher.
[00:53] Priya: 46 percent for KV, okay. I thought KV would be higher — I guess because our sessions include a lot of user-specific items and order ids.
[00:59] Samir: Yeah, exactly. The KV cache is strongly sensitive to the composition of the key — we observed many keys included raw order numbers and user names in the prefix for NovaRetail, so we'll want to normalize or hash those out for better reuse.
[01:12] Mark: Quick question — when you say prefix cache do you mean exact-prefix matching or fuzzy matching? because our templates sometimes add small variations.
[01:19] Lena: Good point. Right now the pilot runs canonical prefix matching: we canonicalize whitespace, lowercase, remove some stopwords, and then fingerprint. But we don't do semantic fuzzy matching — that's more expensive and tricky for correctness.
[01:30] Priya: Could fuzzy matching increase false positives? I'm worried about mixing contexts.
[01:34] Lena: It could, yes — especially for multi-turn where context matters. For now canonicalization plus hashing gives good lift without risking context contamination.
[01:42] Aisha: Do you have example before/after for a template?
[01:45] Lena: Yeah I can share. Example: "Customer asked about return policy for order 12345" gets normalized to "customer asked about return policy" and then fingerprinted. So different order numbers collapse.
[01:56] Priya: That helps.
[01:58] Mark: How do you handle personalization tokens? e.g., recommended products embedded in prompt.
[02:04] Samir: We recommend stripping or replacing high-entropy personal tokens with placeholders early in the pipeline. Redwood's prep hooks can do that in-line — you control the mapping rules. That preserves privacy and improves hit rate.
[02:15] Mark: OK. Memory / infra question — what's the working set size for the KV cache you observed? we need approximate GPU memory and CPU stats.
[02:23] Lena: For the pilot size (about 1500 concurrent sessions peak), the KV working set was roughly 18GB of compressed KV storage across dedicated inference nodes. That scales with session history and sequence length. For a 10k session pilot, estimate ~110-130GB without more aggressive eviction.
[02:39] Mark: Oof — that's higher than we anticipated.
[02:41] Priya: We might need to cap history at 3 turns for production, but for the pilot we can test longer.
[02:47] Lena: TTL and eviction policies are critical here — we can configure LRU-based eviction with per-customer caps; also we support cold-tiering to cheaper nodes if you want longer retention beyond the hot KV.
[02:59] Aisha: Is cold-tiering part of Redwood Dedicated only?
[03:03] Samir: Cold-tiering is available as an option on Dedicated and Private (on-prem) deployments; for hosted we can emulate by storing serialized cache in your S3 or an object store and bring it back into memory on demand, but that has latency tradeoffs.
[03:16] Priya: On the dashboard the prefix hit was 81 but end-to-end latency didn't drop as much as we expected. Why?
[03:23] Lena: Two reasons typically: first, prefix hits reduce generation work but you still pay the overhead of routing and the runtime checks; second, our streaming and KV lookups add small overheads. For small responses the fixed overhead is a bigger percentage. We saw median p95 latency drop from 420ms to 350ms in the best routes, but some long-tail remained due to cold cache pulls.
[03:43] Priya: Got it. The p95 improvement is promising.
[03:46] Mark: Any guidance on composing the cache key? we want to maximize reuse but avoid collisions.
[03:51] Lena: We recommend a conservative key: model+route+normalized_prompt_fingerprint+user_role_bucket (if applicable). Avoid including user_id/order_id. If you need personalization in the model output, you can append a small personalization vector outside the cached prefix and run a short delta decode. That keeps hit rates high for the prefix, and then you do a short personalize step.
[04:13] Samir: Another pattern we've used is two-tier responses: use prefix cache to generate base answer, then run a personalization pass with user tokens — much faster than doing full decode each time.
[04:22] Priya: That pattern might work. Does Redwood support that natively or we implement client-side?
[04:27] Lena: We have native support hooks in the runtime — it's an experimental flow but we can enable it for the pilot. I'll note that as an action.
[04:36] Aisha: About privacy, we need to ensure PII isn't stored in cache. can you scrub before caching?
[04:41] Samir: Yes, scrub rules are configurable. We also support KMS-encrypted cache snapshots and audit logs for cache reads/writes for compliance.
[04:50] Priya: Great — SOC2 stuff on that is important. We'll need the security doc.
[04:54] Samir: I'll attach the SOC2 + data handling whitepaper after the call.
[04:59] Mark: Back to hit rates — the dashboard shows big variance by route, can you walk through the top three performing routes?
[05:04] Lena: Sure — route support-chat: prefix hit 81% (KV 52%), route faq-bot: prefix 88% (KV 63%), route order-tracking: prefix 64% (KV 31%) — order tracking is lower because many queries include receipt/order IDs.
[05:20] Priya: So order-tracking is the main pain. we can probably change UX to mitigate, e.g., pass order id as metadata not in the prompt.
[05:27] Mark: We can change frontend — but that needs product approval. Aisha?
[05:30] Aisha: We can prototype a change for the pilot, yes.
[05:33] Samir: Perfect. One more thing — we also tried a small experiment with prompt templates that reuse canned sentences and got a +6 to +9 percentage points on prefix hits. So prompt engineering is low-hanging fruit.
[05:45] Priya: Nice. Can you share a before/after of the template we should use?
[05:49] Lena: I'll upload examples to the shared folder.
[05:52] Priya: Cool.
[05:53] Samir: Now on KV TTLs — what are your retention constraints?
[05:57] Mark: For compliance, we prefer not to store PII beyond 30 days, but session-level ephemeral data can be shorter, like 7 days. Budget-wise we don't want to exceed 200GB hot memory.
[06:07] Lena: For that constraint, we recommend per-customer cap of ~120GB hot KV and LRU eviction with TTL 7 days for session history; older than that moves to cold tier if needed. We'll run the benchmark to estimate.
[06:19] Priya: If we cap at 3 turns, how much hit rate do we lose?
[06:22] Lena: Preliminary estimate from our sample: capping to 3 turns reduces KV hit from 46% to about 38% but prefix hit remains similar. So tradeoff there.
[06:33] Samir: Another lever is to aggressive-normalize prompts to increase prefix reuse so KV dependence drops.
[06:39] Mark: About benchmarks — what's realistic number of requests we should test for pilot?
[06:43] Samir: For meaningful results, 100k requests across routes with production-like interleaving is good. Lena suggested that earlier.
[06:50] Aisha: How long will that take?
[06:52] Lena: We can run in a couple hours if we provision burst capacity; collecting logs and aggregating might add time. I'll aim to complete within 48 hours of running.
[07:02] Priya: OK. Please include the raw request/response pairs (sanitized) so we can validate.
[07:07] Samir: Yep, we'll sanitize and hash out PII tokens before sharing.
[07:11] Mark: Instrumentation question — can you break down token-level cost savings vs per-request overhead? finance wants numbers.
[07:18] Lena: Yes — from the pilot, token generation cost dropped by ~38% on prefix-hit requests; however per-request infra overhead only moved cost down ~10% because of fixed routing costs. We'll provide a spreadsheet that ties hit rates to expected cost delta at scale.
[07:33] Priya: Good. Send that to finance.
[07:36] Samir: We'll attach a cost model and the workbook.
[07:39] Aisha: On the implementation side, do we need changes in our client or can Redwood handle transparently?
[07:44] Lena: Minimal client changes recommended: a prep hook to normalize prompts and a flag to enable two-pass decode if you want personalization. Rest can be runtime-configured.
[07:54] Priya: OK. We'll scope the prep hook work with our eng team.
[07:58] Mark: Any noted regressions from prefix caching on answer quality?
[08:02] Lena: We ran automated evals on the pilot set — no significant regressions in the top-line metrics. A few edge cases with highly personalized prompts needed the personalization pass. We'll include sample failures in the report.
[08:15] Priya: Good.
[08:16] Samir: Quick recap and next steps: Lena runs the 100k benchmark with prefix caching and TTL=24h initially, Samir will share hit-rate dashboard and security docs, Mark to share retention numbers, and we'll reconvene 2026-07-14. Anything else?
[08:31] Aisha: Please add the template examples to the shared folder.
[08:34] Lena: Will do.
[08:36] Priya: Also include the prompt fingerprinting algorithm description — just high-level.
[08:40] Lena: Yep, I will add that.
[08:42] Samir: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[08:44] Mark: Thanks.
[08:45] Priya: Bye.

--- End transcript ---
